title: Self-directed hypothesis loop
description: With no objective given, the engine surveys the booted schema, forms testable hypotheses about bound columns, tests each as a RelOp chain (dummy ticket first, verdict from live rows), derives new hypotheses from what it learned (drill into a supported slice, try to refute by generalising to peers), and remembers every test so nothing is re-run. A hypothesis is a descriptive statistical statement with a declared threshold. It is never a causal claim. The SLM may only propose bound names; it never writes SQL.

kinds.statement: The leading {dimension} accounts for at least {p:.0%} of total {measure}.
kinds.verdict: share of the top row >= p

kinds.statement: {measure} for {dimension} = {value} is at least {ratio}x the peer mean across {dimension}.
kinds.verdict: value / peer >= ratio for the named row

kinds.statement: Average {measure} is at least {ratio}x higher where {treatment} is above its median.

kinds.verdict: Pearson r over the returned pairs; inconclusive below minPairs

kinds.statement: Total {measure} in {year2} exceeds {year1} by at least {growth:.0%}.

derive.drill: Re-ask the same hypothesis inside the winning slice against another dimension.
derive.refute_peers: Ask the same contrast for a peer value. If the peer also passes, the original is less specific than it looked.
derive.note: Follow-ups are formed from results, not from templates alone. They are still descriptive statements.

verdictNote: supported and refuted come from live rows after a dummy ticket. dummy_only means live replay was disabled, so the verdict is about masked sandbox rows and does not count as evidence. inconclusive means too few rows or a null denominator.

search.note: The strongest supported hypothesis becomes the objective of the atom search in spec/autonomy.json, so the search is directed by evidence rather than by a typed goal.

may: propose extra hypotheses as JSON bound to existing measures, dimensions, and sample values
slm.rejected: any proposal naming a column that does not resolve

honesty: Hypotheses are descriptive statements over bound columns with declared thresholds. Verdicts are threshold comparisons on live RelOp rows, uncorrected for multiple comparisons. Identification is none; nothing here is a causal claim, a forecast, or investment advice.
